b086: Vivid dreams and increased sensitivity to psychedelics are the hoped-for benefits of UMP. That means you should not take the old high doses of your psychedelic at first, as it might hit you way harder than you expected.
b091: If you're sensitive, start lower and do the trial with just 50mg 5-HTP at night for 2–3 nights, then go up to 100mg if 50mg was clearly helpful and not causing side effects. You can also add 10–20mg P5P in the morning, like Scott did, especially if the 5-HTP felt like it "almost worked," as that could be a sign it wasn't converting cleanly over to serotonin. Don't do the trial at the same time as the other suggested regimen changes (like UMP, agmatine, D-serine, psychedelics, or prescription medication changes), since the point is to see whether the 5-HTP itself is doing anything. If it's the right tool, the first things you'll usually notice are your mood or sleep quality improves, you have less nighttime rumination, and your dreams become more vivid or memorable.
p085-086h:
Side effects / stop signs: In practice, the most common problem is the "choline headache", or a spaced-out kind of brain fog. That isn't shown in the studies I've seen, but the likely reason is that UMP speeds up neuronal and synaptic membrane synthesis, which places a higher demand on choline than what people may normally get from diet alone. Other stop signs include insomnia, jitteriness, racing thoughts, irritability, emotional flatness, nausea, stomach cramps, or loose stools.
